definitions.explanation: a written note to help remember something or record information
a formal but non-binding agreement between parties outlining terms and conditions

examples.japanese: {覚書|おぼえがき}を{作|つく}っておく。
examples.english: I'll make a note to remember.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{内容|ないよう}を{覚書|おぼえがき}にまとめた。
examples.english: I summarized the meeting contents in a memo.

examples.japanese: {打|う}ち{合|あ}わせの{前|まえ}に{覚書|おぼえがき}を{読|よ}み{返|かえ}した。
examples.english: I reread my notes before the meeting.

examples.japanese: {両社|りょうしゃ}は{業務|ぎょうむ}{提携|ていけい}に{関|かん}する{覚書|おぼえがき}を{締結|ていけつ}した。
examples.english: Both companies signed a memorandum of understanding regarding their business partnership.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{相手|あいて}{国|こく}と{経済|けいざい}{協力|きょうりょく}の{覚書|おぼえがき}を{交|か}わした。
examples.english: The government exchanged a memorandum of understanding on economic cooperation with the other country.

examples.japanese: {覚書|おぼえがき}は{正式|せいしき}な{契約|けいやく}とは{異|こと}なり、{法的|ほうてき}{拘束力|こうそくりょく}がない{場合|ばあい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Unlike a formal contract, a memorandum of understanding often has no legal binding force.

notes:
{覚書|おぼえがき} has two main uses: personal notes/memos and formal memoranda of understanding.

WRITING:
- {覚|おぼ}える (to remember, memorize)
- {書|が}き (writing)

SENSE 1 - PERSONAL NOTES:
- Used for informal notes to oneself
- Similar to メモ but slightly more formal

SENSE 2 - BUSINESS/LEGAL MOU:
- Less binding than a formal contract
- Used to record preliminary agreements
- Common in international business and diplomacy

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {覚書|おぼえがき}を{交|か}わす (to exchange memoranda)
- {覚書|おぼえがき}を{締結|ていけつ}する (to conclude an MOU)
- {覚書|おぼえがき}に{署名|しょめい}する (to sign an MOU)

RELATED WORDS:
- メモ (memo - informal)
- {契約書|けいやくしょ} (contract - more binding)
- {合意書|ごういしょ} (agreement document)
